title: rosa canina subvar. euoxyphylla
intro: Rosa canina subvar. euoxyphylla, commonly known as the Dwarf Dog Rose, is a subspecies of the Rosa canina plant, a type of wild rose native to Europe. The Dwarf Dog Rose has been traditionally used to support digestive health, reducing inflammation and relieving symptoms associated with gastrointestinal issues, such as bloating and nausea. Its therapeutic actions are primarily due to its anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic properties, which contribute to its potential use in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of the Dwarf Dog Rose include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenes, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
